stimulus.text:
Black population of the United States, counted by the federal census:

| Year | Enslaved people | Free Black people |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1790 | 697,681 | 59,527 |
| 1800 | 893,602 | 108,435 |
| 1820 | 1,538,022 | 233,634 |
| 1840 | 2,487,355 | 386,293 |

Congress banned the importation of enslaved people from abroad, effective January 1, 1808.
stimulus.source_note: Data table from the United States federal census, 1790-1840: free and enslaved Black population. Totals checked against the Census Bureau's Negro Population 1790-1915 and Gannett, Statistics of the Negroes in the United States (1894).

source: original; data table from the United States federal census, 1790-1840
stem: Comparing the two columns, which of the following is best supported by the table?

options.text: Free Black people had finally outnumbered enslaved people by the time of the 1840 census
options.misconception: In 1840 the enslaved numbered about 2.5 million and the free about 386,000.

options.text: Free numbers grew faster, but the enslaved still outnumbered them six to one in 1840
The free Black population grew only in the North
options.misconception: The table gives national totals only; it shows no regional split.

options.text: Both groups stopped growing after the importation ban of 1808

rationales.A: The free never outnumbered the enslaved. In 1840 the enslaved were about 2.5 million and the free about 386,000.
rationales.B: The free grew more than sixfold and the enslaved more than threefold, yet the enslaved still outnumbered the free by more than six to one.
rationales.C: The table counts the whole country. It cannot show where the free population grew.
rationales.D: Neither group stopped growing. Both columns rise at every census after 1808.
rationales.general:
1. Compare growth in proportion. The free rose more than sixfold; the enslaved more than threefold.
2. Compare size in 1840. About 2.5 million enslaved people against about 386,000 free, more than six to one.
3. Hold both facts together. Faster growth did not mean larger numbers.
Background: Free Black people were about 8 percent of Black Americans in 1790 and about 13 percent in 1840.
Remember: faster growth and bigger numbers are two different claims; check each one.
